tasks.short: Maintain awareness of medicine, rules, and insurance.

steps.what: List stored government regulations
Maintain awareness of advances in medicine
Review computerized diagnostic and treatment equipment
Review health insurance changes and financing options
Sign the awareness note for this month
File the signed awareness note
outputs: filed copy of signed awareness note v1

tasks.design: A job lists stored government regulations in {DOCS}. The manager maintains awareness of advances in medicine, computerized diagnostic and treatment equipment, data processing technology, health insurance changes, and financing options. A later job files the signed note. It does not decide a policy.
tasks.previous_blocker: Regulation titles and insurance notes were forwarded by mail and easy to lose.
tasks.enabler_now: A stored feed can list regulation titles the facility already collects.
tasks.still_hard: A medical advance is not understood by listing its title.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides what the facility will act on.

ambition.what: Review a stored regulation title in the same week it is filed.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on the advance, not on hunting the list.

evidence.claim: The health digest says strategy and people decisions stay manual, with drafting help only, and there is no agent.
Digest [S1] describes a policy library with approvals, where a summary of a rule still waits for a person.

assumptions: The list is titles, not a decision.
Configure the existing store before a new feed.
unknowns: Which insurance changes apply to this facility.
research_questions: How often a financing option never appears in the store.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining reading time is still the manager's own study.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes the feed is sparse. The high end assumes the feed lists the regulations already collected. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Establish work schedules and staff assignments.

steps.what: List workload, space, and equipment availability
Draft a schedule from those constraints
Establish work schedules and staff assignments
Sign the staff schedule for this period
File the signed staff schedule
outputs: filed copy of signed staff schedule v1

tasks.design: A job lists workload, space, and equipment availability from {OPS_SYSTEM} and drafts a schedule in {CALENDAR} from those constraints only. The manager establishes the assignments. No model rosters people by behaviour. A later job files the signed schedule. A vendor time figure is not this saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability was collected by mail, and a roster tool that scores people would need a separate consent.
tasks.enabler_now: Workload, space, and equipment are already recorded.
tasks.still_hard: A person can be unavailable for a reason the constraint pack does not hold.
tasks.human_edge: The manager establishes who works which assignment.

ambition.what: Set the week's assignments from the constraint draft instead of a blank grid.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on the assignment, not on collecting availability.

evidence.claim: The health digest says scheduling is a configured product, working-time rules are constraints, and no model sets the roster.
Digest [S10] says hiring, evaluating, or rostering staff on behaviour or traits is high-risk, and Digest [S11] says those duties apply from 2 December 2027.
Digest [S12] says rosters, staff data, and monitoring need works-council consent, so this design does not watch named staff.
Digest [S4] is a vendor report of shorter shift-planning time, and this design does not use that figure as its own saving.
Digest [S9] says staff decisions must not rest on automation alone, so hiring and evaluation stay with the manager.

assumptions: The draft uses workload, space, and equipment, not behaviour.
Configure the existing calendar before a new roster product.
Works-council consent is a separate decision before any new monitoring.
unknowns: Whether the current calendar is already a consented roster.
Which working-time rules bind the draft.
research_questions: How often equipment availability is wrong.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining assignment time is still the manager deciding.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes constraints are incomplete. The high end assumes constraints are already recorded. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor beds, services, and facility use.

steps.what: Show diagnostic services and inpatient bed counts
Monitor facilities against the stored counts
Assess the need for additional staff and equipment
Sign the resource need for this period
File the signed resource note
outputs: filed copy of signed resource note v1

tasks.design: A job shows diagnostic-service, inpatient-bed, and facility counts in {BI}. The manager monitors that use and assesses the need for additional staff, equipment, and services. The view does not score named staff. A later job files the signed note in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bed and service counts were copied into a sheet before anyone could judge capacity.
tasks.enabler_now: Those counts are already in the booking record.
tasks.still_hard: Need can turn on a clinical limit the count does not show.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides whether more staff, equipment, or services are needed.

ambition.what: Judge capacity the day the bed count is on the page.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on the need, not on copying counts.

evidence.claim: The health digest says budgets and reports are generated from the booking record, and any commentary is checked against the figures.
Digest [S12] says rosters, staff data, and monitoring need works-council consent, so this design does not watch named staff.
Digest [S10] says hiring, evaluating, or rostering staff on behaviour or traits is high-risk, and Digest [S11] says those duties apply from 2 December 2027.

assumptions: Counts are by service and bed, not by a person's behaviour.
Configure the existing booking record before a new store.
unknowns: Which services are in the booking record.
research_questions: How often a bed count lags the ward.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining review time is still the manager's assessment.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes counts lag the ward. The high end assumes counts are stored the same day. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List open posts and blank application fields
Direct recruitment and hiring of personnel
Conduct training of hired personnel
Sign the hiring decision for this post
File the signed hiring decision
outputs: filed copy of signed hiring decision v1

tasks.design: A job lists open posts and blank application fields in {ATS}. It does not rank or score anyone. The manager directs recruitment and hiring, and conducts the training. A later job files the signed decision in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Application packs were incomplete, and a ranking tool would have made the hiring decision.
tasks.enabler_now: The application record can show blank fields.
tasks.still_hard: Hiring still depends on the conversation and the references.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides who is hired and whether the training is enough.

ambition.what: Start the hiring conversation once required fields are present.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on hiring and training, not on chasing blank fields.

evidence.claim: Digest [S9] says staff decisions must not rest on automation alone, so hiring and evaluation stay with the manager.
Digest [S10] says hiring, evaluating, or rostering staff on behaviour or traits is high-risk, and Digest [S11] says those duties apply from 2 December 2027.
The health digest says strategy and people decisions stay manual, with drafting help only, and there is no agent.

assumptions: Blank fields are not a ranking.
Configure the existing application record before a new tool.
unknowns: Who else must approve a hire.
Which training is mandatory before a start date.
research_questions: How often a required field is not on the form.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining hiring time is still the manager's decision.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes applications are often incomplete. The high end assumes required fields are usually present. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The health services manager spends the week on the unit, the people, and the signed decision. A schedule draft and a filed report can move. No model hires, evaluates, rosters, or sends a calamity report.
reach: A department head sees the schedule only after the manager signs it.
Finance receives the fiscal note the manager signed, not a generated rate.
skills_to_grow: Reject a report figure that has no source row.
Keep hiring, evaluation, and the roster as their own decision.
role.ambitious_version: A signed report or policy can be filed the same day, and the manager still decides it.
